finding.claim: Authorization bypass in the ban endpoint. The require_admin() call is wrapped in try/except Exception. abort(403) raises werkzeug HTTPException, which is an Exception subclass, so the except block catches it and only logs a warning. Execution continues to do_ban(uid) and returns ok=True. Any authenticated non-admin user can ban any user. The same happens if g.user is missing or malformed, because the resulting AttributeError/TypeError is also swallowed. The unban endpoint calls require_admin without the try/except and is correctly protected, so ban is inconsistent with it.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user (g.user without is_admin) sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, the privileged ban operation

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban accepts POST, uid is attacker-chosen
require_admin(g.user) is called; for a non-admin it calls abort(403) at line 11, raising HTTPException
except Exception catches the HTTPException, so the 403 is never returned
Only a warning is logged; there is no re-raise or return
do_ban(uid) runs unconditionally and the handler returns 200 ok=True

finding.guards_checked: require_admin checks is_admin, but its failure is swallowed by the try/except. There is no other decorator, before_request hook, or middleware in the repo (the only file is admin.py). The unban route (line 26) has no try/except, so it is not affected. The log line only records g.user name and is not a control.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 but is called inside try/except Exception (admin.py:16-19), which swallows the HTTPException; no other decorator, hook or middleware exists.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17-20 the abort(403) from require_admin (line 11) is caught by `except Exception` and only logged, so do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs for any non-admin user, unlike unban at line 26. One detail in the claim is wrong: if g.user is missing, the log call at line 19 raises again and the request fails with a 500, so that sub-case does not bypass the check.
